revisions.desc: first delivery: 4 breeds, 16-bit back view (21 rows), 8-bit road walk/idle, hitching rail 48x20.

changes: 1 cape hid the horse: new short MOUNTED cape for green / fur / oilskin (back: hem at the belt, half-width 12.8 art px vs 18.8; front: narrow panel ending at the saddle); every breed widened at the hips (bx 1.06-1.18, hindquarter scale "quarters") so the barrel and rump show on both sides of the rider.

2 cob read small: broader deep barrel (bx 1.06, by 1.26), heavy rounded hindquarters (quarters 1.22, raised croup), thicker neck; 8-bit cob body widened 2 px with a heavier rump (seat anchor (14,19), was (14,20)).

3 sword over the neck/head in idle: mounted idle/hit now carry every weapon upright beside the shoulder from a hand on the thigh (crossbow hangs prod-down); hit keeps it upright; death lets it fall back/down; destrier neck carried forward and the hit head-toss no longer throws the neck into the rider. Measured overlap in verification.weaponOverHorse.

4 rout row (row 21, both views) and a FRONT view (enemy side, horse facing screen-left) with every row; generic enemy rider = P1 light-horse rider kit on the P7 grid (battle16/rider/lighthorse-rider-{back,front}.png, battle16.genericRider).
5 hitching rail 64x20 (was 48x20), tie rings at x 15 and 50 (35 px apart, was 19), strict NES; 8-bit muzzle anchors added per breed/frame to line a horse up with a ring.

BREAKING for the game: battle16.breeds -> battle16.views[view].breeds; rider sheets are keyed per view (items[slot][variant].sheets[view][...], P5 style). File names of the back view keep the rev-1 scheme with "-back".
1 mace (and axe) idle carry: hang head-down at the knee, clear of every breed's head (min gap >= 4 px; the destrier head is the tallest).

2 bow, front: slung on the back in the front sheet (string and limb beside the rider, not over the face or lap); back sheet keeps the upright carry. Front-sheet bow draws are drawn on the far side of the body.
3 crossbow: slung on the back, prod up, unspanned (both views; reads as a crossbow T over the cape instead of a triangle at the knee).

4 windup/attack/recover re-pathed (src/horses/mwpn.py): melee cocked back over the shoulder and delivered forward-high above the head, spear overarm, bow canted and raised, crossbow aimed up; ranged rows carry the horse head low and forward. 0 weapon px over the head on every frame; remaining neck px only at the withers where the hand sits (see verification.weaponOverHorse.rev3).

5 death: the weapon leaves the hand on frame 1 (tumbling behind the rider, clear of horse and rider) and is gone from frame 2; generic rider: the lance leaves the hand (flung free on frame 2, empty hand from frame 2).
6 generic-rider reins: new horse sheets genericRider.horseSheets[view][breed] with the reins ending in the generic rider's rein hand (drawn on top of his torso in his sheet), every frame and view.
7 8-bit: short seated cape layers road8/walker-cloak-seated-{green,fur,oilskin}.png replace the walker cloak when mounted.
8 cob size unchanged (intended smallest breed). Grid, rows, frame sizes, anchors and riderOffset unchanged; additive JSON keys only.

1 death: the weapon falls instead of being thrown - slips from the hand on frame 1, short downward arc past the rump, near the ground on frame 3, lying on frame 4 (spear: out of frame); never over horse or rider. Generic rider: the lance slips on frame 2, falls past the rump on frame 3, out of frame on frame 4.

2 front-view sword/axe/mace windups re-pathed (src/horses/mwpn.py MWPN_FRONT): weapon held up beside the hood in front of the body, rider leaning back; front windup horse head a little lower. Whole weapon visible, hand + hilt >= 4 px from neck/head.
3 front-view slung bow diagonal across the back (both limbs beside the body), slung crossbow prod over the near shoulder with the stock beside the hood; strings behind the hood and torso.

4 back-view slung bow shorter and higher on the cape (lower limb ends at the belt, 0 px over the horse); the bow is now slung in every shared row of the back sheet too (rev 3 carried it upright in the hand there; it vanished in death).
5 front-view idle: spear sloped back over the far shoulder behind the body; sword lowered point-back across the thigh.
6 generic-rider reins: the last 3 px run level into the glove from the horse's side (lancer horse sheets only).
7 8-bit: seated capes back to the walker width (still short, hem row 15); new seated belt lanterns road8/walker-lantern-seated-{standard,hooded}.png at the hip.

8 generic enemy rider drawn x1.10 (was ~90% of the mounted Warden); the main cause of the in-game size gap is game-side (BattleScene.js scales foe riders by 0.78 x 1.25 vs the Warden's 1.25), see gameSideChanges.

cob.desc: stocky dun (rev 2: broader and heavier): short legs (0.90), heavy bone (1.42), deep barrel (1.26) as long as the palfrey's, heavy rounded hindquarters (1.22) with a raised croup, short thick neck, broad short head, hogged dark mane, full tail, feathered fetlocks, dark points + dorsal stripe.

palfrey.desc: the reference riding horse (P1 light-horse build): dapple grey, long pale mane falling down the neck, long flowing tail.

courser.desc: lean chestnut: long legs (1.10), fine bone (0.84), long shallow barrel with a tucked belly, long fine neck, fine long head with a white blaze, flaxen mane, tail carried high.

destrier.desc: big black-brown warhorse: long deep barrel (1.18 x 1.26), heavy bone (1.42), thick arched crest carried forward (rev 2), big head, white socks + white feathering, crimson caparison with brass trim and roundel, steel chanfron, war saddle with a high cantle.

back.facing: horse faces screen-RIGHT, rider seen from behind (player side, bottom-left)

front.facing: horse faces screen-LEFT, rider seen from the front (enemy side, top-right)

battle16.viewNote: rev 2: two views on the SAME grid and row order. back = player side (as rev 1), front = enemy side (new). Mounted figures are drawn at x1.25 in battle (Ronja), so 280x256 frames show at 350x320 on screen; scale the whole composited frame about the ground anchor.

anchor.desc: ground point between the hooves (hooves on row 250, 6 px margin as P1 214/220). Every horse sheet and every rider sheet (both views) uses this same frame grid.

battle16.whyNot220: P1 is 220x220; the Warden is taller than the P1 rider (hood + helmet, weapons raised overhead, spear/bow upright) and the destrier carries him higher, and the courser lunge / falling horse is longer. 280x256 keeps every pixel of every breed x loadout x frame x view inside the frame (export16.py asserts it). Same scale as P1, just more room.

animationNotes.rows: same row names and frame counts as the P5 rows (warden-gear.json). Rows 0-20 are unchanged from rev 1; rev 2 appends rout as row 21 (P5 has rout as row 3: look rows up by name, not index). Horse rows and rider rows always have the same index and length; play horse frame f with rider frame f.
animationNotes.idle: loops: horse breathes (neck/head/tail), rider idles with the weapon hand on the thigh close to the body. Carry (rev 4): back rig: sword and spear upright beside the shoulder; front rig: spear sloped back over the far shoulder behind the hood, sword lowered point-back across the thigh (nothing in front of the torso or face); axe and mace hang head-down at the knee; bow and crossbow are slung on the back in EVERY shared row of both sheets (front: bow diagonal across the back with both limbs showing beside him, crossbow prod over the near shoulder with the stock beside the hood; back: bow short and high on the cape, crossbow over the cape). No weapon touches the horse's head on any breed (verification.weaponOverHorse.rev4).
animationNotes.hit: frame 0 = brightness flash on horse AND rider (inside the ramps). rev 2: the horse tosses its head up with the neck kept forward (rev 1 threw the whole neck back into the weapon); the weapon stays upright, tipped back.
animationNotes.death: 5 frames: flinch (flash), forelegs buckle, down on the knees, collapse, lying. The rider slumps forward in the saddle. rev 4: the weapon FALLS (rev 3 jumped ~100 px in one frame and read as a throw): frame 0 still in the hand, the arm thrown back, weapon tipped up and back over the croup; frame 1 it slips out of the opening hand just behind it; frame 2 it falls past the rump; frame 3 near the ground beside the hind quarters; frame 4 lying on the ground (spear: fallen out of the frame). Frames 1-4 have 0 weapon px over the horse (all breeds) and over the rider (verification.weaponOverHorse.rev4.*.death). Slung bow / crossbow stay strapped on (both sheets). The belt lantern stays on the belt.
animationNotes.rout: rev 2, 4 frames, both views: frame 0 = the horse wheels (rears on the hind legs) in the sheet's own view, frames 1-3 = gallop AWAY drawn in the OPPOSITE view (back sheet: horse faces screen-left, rider seen from the front = running toward screen-left; front sheet: horse faces screen-right, rider seen from behind). Play once, then loop frames 1-3 while the unit leaves (same as P1 / P5 rout). views[view].rig.rout / horseFacing.rout list the rig + facing per frame; the rider parts of frames 1-3 are the "@<other view>" parts in layerOrder (P5 convention).
animationNotes.melee: sword/spear/axe/mace: the horse gathers (forehand up) in windup and lunges into the blow with the hind hooves planted (P1 lunge). rev 3 arcs: cocked up and back over the shoulder in windup, swung over the top, delivered forward-HIGH above the horse's head (cavalry cut / overarm spear thrust), never across the neck or head. The last recover frame settles into the idle carry. rev 4, FRONT sheet sword/axe/mace windup: the weapon is held up beside the hood in front of the body (rev 3 hid it behind the hood), the rider leans back and the gathering horse keeps its head a little lower (front sheet only), so the whole weapon shows (minVisible 1.0) and hand + hilt clear the neck/head by >= 4 px on every breed.
animationNotes.ranged: bow/crossbow: the horse stands steady for the shot with its head carried low and forward (rev 3), a small start at the loose. rev 3: short canted mounted bow draw raised above the head (front sheet: the bow is in the far hand, drawn behind the body so the string never crosses the face); crossbow raised to the cheek and aimed up over the head. Both hands are on the weapon, so the reins are knotted on the neck in those rows (drawn in the horse sheet).

battle16.seatAnchorRule: views[view].breeds[b].seatAnchors[row][f] = output px of the saddle seat in that horse frame. riderSeat = the same point in every rider frame (both views, Warden and generic rider). riderOffset[row][f] = seatAnchors - riderSeat (always even, so the rider stays on the 2x2 art-pixel grid). Draw rider frame f at (horse frame x + dx, y + dy).

green.note: rev 2: MOUNTED cape. back:cape and front:drape are the short riding cape (hem at the belt, no wider than the torso) so the horse stays visible; hood + front mantle are the P5 ones. Same variant keys as P5.

fur.note: rev 2: MOUNTED cape. back:cape and front:drape are the short riding cape (hem at the belt, no wider than the torso) so the horse stays visible; hood + front mantle are the P5 ones. Same variant keys as P5.

oilskin.note: rev 2: MOUNTED cape. back:cape and front:drape are the short riding cape (hem at the belt, no wider than the torso) so the horse stays visible; hood + front mantle are the P5 ones. Same variant keys as P5.

standard-belt.note: mounted: the lantern always hangs on the belt (the off hand holds the reins). Map a hand lantern "<v>" to "<v>-belt".

hooded-belt.note: mounted: the lantern always hangs on the belt (the off hand holds the reins). Map a hand lantern "<v>" to "<v>-belt".

anchors.units: output px inside the RIDER frame (add riderOffset for the horse frame)

mountedCape.back: cape from the shoulders to the belt (hem at local y -27.6, was -15 on foot), max half-width 12.8 art px (P5 cape 18.8)
mountedCape.front: the panel behind the body shows only beside the arms (half-width 16, P5 22.4) and ends at the saddle
mountedCape.variants: green / fur (tufted hem + fur collar) / oilskin (straight waxed hem): same superset rule as P5, so the layer cut stays exact

mountedCarry.note: rig-local art px / degrees (0 = blade up). P5 on foot: hand (-18, -31), sword 200 (hanging forward). rev 4: frontRigCarry overrides the sword/spear carry in front-rig frames (site w_back = behind the body); slung = bow / crossbow strapped on the back in every shared row (upper-body coords).

rider.source: src/horses/rider16.py: the P5 Warden rig seated (near leg only, plate greave near leg only, short mounted cape, upright mounted carry), cut with src/warden/layers.py (same layer-safe shading, sites, parts and outline rules as P5).
rider.reuse: Same item keys, variants and qualities as P5 warden-gear.json; sheets are keyed per view exactly like warden-gear.json (items[slot][variant].sheets[view]["<view>:<part>"], plus "outline"). Mounted sheets are a separate set because the legs, cape and hand positions differ.

genericRider.kit: P1 Light Horse rider (incoming/P1-light-horse; src/kits.py "horse": padded jack, cap, lance, cloth1 sleeves) drawn ALONE on the P7 grid with its seat on riderSeat, so enemy (and P1 light-horse) riders can switch to any P7 breed.
genericRider.horseSheetsNote: rev 3: draw the generic rider on THESE horse sheets (battle16/horse-<breed>-<view>-lancer.png, same grid, rows, seatAnchors and riderOffset as views[view].breeds[breed]); their reins end in the generic rider's rein hand (genericRider.anchors[view][row][f].reinHand). The standard sheets end the reins at the Warden's off hand, which sat under the lance hand. Rows the generic rider never uses are copies of the standard sheet.
genericRider.animationNotes: the lance plays on the SPEAR rows (P1 windup 2 / attack 3 / death 4 re-timed to the P7 3 / 4 / 5 by key interpolation); every other weapon row of the sheet is empty. Lance sloped up/back except windup 1 + attack (couched), as P1. Death: frames 0-1 held, the hand is empty from frame 2 (as rev 3). rev 4: the lance FALLS - frame 2 it slips out of the hand tipping back over the croup, frame 3 it drops past the rump head-down toward the ground, frame 4 it has fallen out of the frame; 0 lance px over the rider or any horse in frames 2-4.
genericRider.composite: horse frame from genericRider.horseSheets[view][breed] (rev 3), then the generic rider frame at riderOffset (one sheet: it carries its own outline).
genericRider.scale: rev 4: drawn x1.10 about the seat (P1 kit rider_scale 1.0 made him ~90% of the hooded mounted Warden: seat-to-crown 94 vs 104 px, shoulders ~64 vs ~70 px). Now 102 vs 104 px and within ~3% across the shoulders, same seat anchor, rows, frame counts and anchors; the lancer horse sheets hang the stirrup under his boot.
genericRider.factions: the rider uses the P1 ramps (cloth1 jack, cloth2, leather, metal, skin, hair, wood), so the P1 faction palette swaps apply to this sheet unchanged.

compositeRule: 2. rider (at riderOffset): outline sheets first: rider.body[view].outline, then each worn slot's outline in rider.outlineOrder
3. rider.body[view].content, then walk rider.layerOrder: "<slot>.<part>" -> items[slot][variant].sheets[view][part] if worn and present (hood colours replace cloak hood parts with the same key)
2-3 are exactly the P5 warden-gear.json rule (heroArt.js sheetsFor) with view = the sheet view. Nothing of the rider goes under the horse.
generic enemy rider: genericRider.horseSheets[view][breed] for 1 (rev 3) and genericRider.sheets[view] instead of 2-3.
battle16.tack: saddle, saddle cloth (destrier: caparison + steel chanfron), bridle, reins (bit -> rein hand, or knotted on the neck in bow/crossbow rows) and the stirrup under the boot are all in the horse sheet.

anchor.desc: bottom-centre, hooves on row 35 (origin 0.5, 1 as the game uses now)

road8.muzzleRule: muzzle[frame] = rightmost head pixel (x, y) in the 32x36 frame (horse faces right; mirror x -> 31 - x when flipped). To tie a horse: place it so muzzle lands 1-2 px beside a prop tie ring.
road8.rev2: cob rebuilt broader with heavier hindquarters (seat anchors moved 1 px up: (14,19) idle / (14,18) on walk B and D); other breeds unchanged.

rider.rule: seated rider = the P5 walker layer strips (incoming/P5-warden-gear/walkers8/layers) cut at frame B (x 16-31), with layers/walker-body.png replaced by road8/walker-body-seated.png and (rev 3) the cloak layer replaced by road8/walker-cloak-seated-<cloak>.png (rider.cloak[cloak]: short seated cape, hem under the belt at row 15, rev 4: walker width, = the 16-bit short mounted cape) and (rev 4) the lantern layer replaced by road8/walker-lantern-seated-<standard|hooded>.png (rider.lantern[variant], on the belt at the hip; any lamp key "<v>" or "<v>-belt" -> variant <v>). Paste the 16x22 result so riderSeat lands on seatAnchors[frame] (rider pixel (9,15) = hip on the saddle).
rider.otherRiders: any 16x22 walker: take rows 0-16 of its frame B, draw road8/walker-leg-seated.png over it (rows 17-21), and paste at seatAnchors - (9,15). Replaces the "upper 60%" crop in mount8.js.

prop.desc: rev 2: hitching rail with a water trough, 64x20 (was 48x20; oak posts O/D, iron tie rings s/S, water u/v/B). Tie rings near the ends, 35 px apart (was 19), so two 32 px horses tied nose-to-ring side by side both show and the rail stays visible between them. Ground row 19 (anchor bottom-centre).

road8.checked: every pixel of every 8-bit PNG is an exact reference/nes-palette.js colour, alpha 0/255, Y/y never used; 60480 mounted composites (4 breeds x 8 frames x 3 cloaks x 5 helmets x 6 weapons x shields x armour x hood/lantern) rebuilt from the saved PNGs = direct in-code mount: 0 mismatches.

palette.note: every opaque 16-bit pixel is a colour of these ramps or one of the 2 outline colours; alpha only 0/255. The 12 horse ramps are new (no colour shared with any other ramp). Warden ramps are unchanged from P5.

nesMapping.paletteSource: reference/nes-palette.js (exact colours only; alpha 0 or 255; no anti-aliasing)

skin.why: as P1: face T, shade a, R only for the deepest crease.

hair.why: as P1: one flat D mass under the hood.

leather.why: as P1: boots, belt, straps D; O only as a highlight.

wood.why: as P1: shafts and hafts O with a K underside, C glint.

metal.why: as P1: steel S/s with a w glint. On the walker only "good"/"fine" steel gets the w glint (see iron).

cloak.why: Warden green hood + cloak = G body with n for the inner shadow of the hood. Rev 2 (Ronja: the Warden stays green): the Warden owns G and n, and the g highlight was dropped so the Warden never uses a Covenant key. The Covenant moves to t/g/l (see covenant-green-proposal.json).

tunic.why: olive tunic/arm wraps. NES has no desaturated olive, and G would merge with the cloak, so it is grey S like the P1 cloth2 hose. The 16-bit colour stays olive (dE is high, noted).

hose.why: dark hose K with S where lit. Legs read as dark, and the D boots split them from the K outline.

jerkin.why: brown leather jerkin D, lifted to O on the lit edge. It is one step apart from hair D, but the hood face-opening separates them.

glow.why: lantern light apricot a, with a C/w core and an E rim. Y/y (the Lab-nearest) are League gold and are kept free.

iron.why: basic weapons: grey S with a K shade and never a w glint. Good/fine steel (metal ramp) gets the w glint, so quality still reads at 8-bit.

brass.why: fine fittings = O with a C glint (like P2 gilt). y is avoided (League).

gambeson.why: padded armour: tan O with C quilting lines, same language as the P1 tan jack. The 16-bit ramp was warmed from grey khaki so both tiers agree.

furcloak.why: warm fur cloak: D body, O tips, C frost glint. The 16-bit ramp was warmed from grey-brown to fox brown so it reads warm and maps to D/O.

oilskin.why: oilskin: slate S body with K folds and an s sheen streak. The 16-bit ramp was shifted from olive-brown to slate so it maps to S and cannot merge with the D jerkin.

paint.why: as P1: kite shield face E, shade R, glint a (same ramp as the troop shields).

patchwool.why: patched hood: worn brown wool, O body with D shade (lighter than the D hair so the face opening still reads). Patches use the tunic (S) and gambeson (O/C) mappings.

mossweave.why: Mossweave Cowl (Covenant piece) = the proposed Covenant jade: t shade, g body, l light. Never G/n (Warden).

nightglass.why: Nightglass Hood (Nightglass piece) = indigo p body, violet P light, K shade (the Nightglass keys).

fleece.why: sheepskin and hare fur: cream C with an O shade, D/K underside.

outline.why: as P1: both outline rings become black K.

dun.why: cob: yellow dun = O body, D shade (game placeholder: body O, dark D).

hpoint.why: dark points (mane, tail, lower legs of the cob and destrier): K, D where lit.

grey.why: palfrey: dapple grey = s body, S shade + S dapples (game placeholder s/S).

silver.why: palfrey mane + tail: w with s strands.

chestnut.why: courser: bright chestnut = E body, R shade. Deliberately lighter/oranger than the P1 light horse (R body) so the two never read as the same horse.

flax.why: courser flaxen mane + tail: C with O shade.

blackbay.why: destrier: black-brown = D body, K shade (game placeholder D/K).

whitehair.why: white socks (destrier), blaze (courser), destrier feathering: w.

saddlecloth.why: saddle cloth: russet wool R with a brass O edge (never Y/y: League gold).

caparison.why: destrier barding: crimson R with brass O trim, dagged hem and an O roundel on the quarters.

tack.why: saddle, bridle, reins, girth: D, K edges.

nesMapping.avoid: Y/y (League) are never used. Warden colours own G/n; g/l/t only appear on the Covenant Mossweave Cowl and P/p only on the Nightglass Hood (faction pieces). See covenant-green-proposal.json.
nesMapping.dENote: dE = Lab distance (p1_nes.de) from the 16-bit colour to the chosen NES colour.

consistency: Ronja's rule: each breed keeps its build and colours in both tiers — cob short-legged O/D dun with dark points and feathering, palfrey s/S dapple grey with a w mane, courser long-legged E/R chestnut with a C flaxen mane and w blaze, destrier big D/K with w socks, R caparison with O trim and an s chanfron. See preview.png (16-bit row over 8-bit row).

compositeVsDirect.rule: composite from the saved PNGs + horses.json (src/horses/gamecomp16.py, P5 rule) vs direct in-code render of horse + whole rider; every opaque pixel compared (colour + silhouette)

weaponOverHorse.rule: weapon pixels (outline incl.) lying over the horse's neck / head in the composited frame, weapon "good" quality, summed over the 4 breeds and all frames of the row; maxPerFrame = worst single breed frame; minHeadGap = fewest empty px between any weapon px and the horse's head/ears over all breeds and frames (-1 = overlapping, 99 = no weapon drawn); overRiderMax = most weapon px over the rider's own body/cape in one frame (front view: the bow/crossbow carry). Output px. The weapon fist/grip at the rider's side always sits over the neck base (withers), so a few neck px per frame remain by construction.
weaponOverHorse.rev4Rule: rev 4 adds per row: minHandNeckGap = fewest empty px between the weapon OR its hand (the weapon-hand fist, outline incl.) and the horse's neck/mane/head over all breeds and frames (-1 = touching/overlapping; the idle hand rests on the thigh at the withers by construction); minVisible = smallest share of the weapon's own silhouette left visible (not hidden by the rider) in that row (weapon rows only); overHorsePerFrame = weapon px over the horse (worst breed) per frame. genericRiderDeath = the lance in the generic rider's death row: px over the rider and over each breed (lancer sheets) per frame.
weaponOverHorse.slungRule: rev 4: slung bow / crossbow in the shared rows (idle, hit, death, rout; both sheets, both rigs): offRiderPx = weapon px outside the rider's own silhouette (the parts that show beside him), offRiderOverHorse = those of them that lie over the horse (worst breed); must be 0.

gameSideChanges: rev 4 (needed, small): tests/p7-horse-rules.mjs asserts H.revision === 3 and 327 rider layer sheets (JSON and on disk); rev 4 is revision 4 with 315 rider layer sheets (bow no longer drops -> no back bow w_drop; front sword/axe/mace windups and the front sword idle are drawn in front -> no front sword/axe/mace w_back; the back-sheet spear rout frames are drawn behind -> spear "back:w_back@front" replaces "back:w_front@front"). Copy the whole folder (delete stale layer PNGs) and update those two numbers; every other assert of that test holds (bow/crossbow back:w_back@front, front:w_back, no front bow w_front, a w_drop sheet, WEAPON_LEAVES_HAND {warden: 1, generic: 2}, idle seats, seat maths).

rev 4 (game-side fix for item 8, recommended): enemy riders are drawn at roughly half the mounted Warden's size by the game, not by the art. src/scenes/BattleScene.js: makeFigure scales a foe by m = sc * 0.78 (cavFoe sc 0.60 back rank / 0.68 front rank) and toEnemyRider then calls setScale(m * ENEMY_RIDER_SCALE) with ENEMY_RIDER_SCALE = 1.25 -> 0.585 / 0.663 on screen, against MOUNTED_SCALE 1.25 for the mounted Warden (toHeroArt) = 0.47-0.53x. Fix: in toEnemyRider use setScale(sc * ENEMY_RIDER_SCALE) (drop the 0.78 foot-soldier factor for P7 riders: 0.75 / 0.85 = 0.60-0.68x, the same depth-rank ratio the foot units use) or setScale(MOUNTED_SCALE) for parity; widen the cavFoe slot spacing if the larger riders overlap. Design call for Ronja / Gamedev 2. The art side (generic rider x1.10) is already in the sheets and needs no code.

rev 4 (additive, non-breaking): road8 mounted rider -> use road8.rider.lantern[variant] (road8/walker-lantern-seated-<standard|hooded>.png) instead of the P5 walker lantern strip frame B when mounted; the seated capes keep their file names (wider pixels only)

rev 4: nothing breaking - sheets 1400x5632, 5 x 22 grid, 280x256 frames, anchor (140,250), riderSeat, seat anchors, riderOffset, row names/indices, frame counts and fps unchanged; rider.layerOrder unchanged; same weapon sites; death leave-hand frames unchanged (Warden f1, generic f2); weaponTip stays absent/ignored from those frames. A game that walks layerOrder and loads whatever items[slot][variant].sheets lists needs no code change.

rev 3 (additive, non-breaking): generic enemy rider -> draw its horse from battle16.genericRider.horseSheets[view][breed] (battle16/horse-<breed>-<view>-lancer.png, same grid/rows/riderOffset) so the reins end in its hand; the standard sheets still work but show the rein end under the lance hand

rev 3 (additive, non-breaking): road8 mounted rider -> use road8.rider.cloak[cloak] (road8/walker-cloak-seated-<cloak>.png, 16x22, one frame) instead of the P5 walker cloak strip frame B; the rest of the walker layer rule is unchanged

rev 3: no layout change - sheets 1400x5632, 5 x 22 grid, 280x256 frames, anchor (140,250), riderSeat, row names/indices/frame counts and fps all as rev 2; rider.layerOrder is unchanged (85 entries, no new slots). The slung bow/crossbow and the dropped weapon use existing weapon sites, so some weapon variants gained "<view>:w_drop" / "<view>:w_back" sheets and bow/crossbow lost their "<view>:w_front" sheets (rider layer sheets 294 -> 327).
